title: Jeremy Thomas
text:
Welcome to my website!



My name is Jeremy Thomas and I’m a PhD Neuroscience candidate at the University of British Columbia, with a research focus on Computational Neuroscience. I’m particularly interested in modelling human behaviour as probabilistic inference, and focus on questions like how cognition is involved in motor skill learning. The desired outcome with this research is an increased ability to intervene in the human sensorimotor system for health and disease.
I am also like to do fun side-projects and apply the computational tools that I use in my research to business use cases.
Have a look at samples of my work on the Projects page!

title: Projects
text:
GitHub Repository
Python · Classification · Regression

Built an end-to-end modeling pipeline to predict product adoption across 25,000+ merchants using 1.5M+ transaction-level time-series observations.
Engineered temporal behavioural features from transactional time-series data (e.g., usage consistency and variability)..
Benchmarked regularized logistic regression against XGBoost using cross-validation, showing comparable predictive performance with improved interpretability.
Ranked the top 10–15% of merchants for targeted marketing and used model coefficients to identify key drivers of subscription adoption.

What I’d do next

Predict product adoption timing using survival based approaches rather than static classification

Validate targeting strategies via offline backtesting paired with online experimentation assumptions





Python · Experimentation · Unsupervised Learning

Designed and analyzed a large-scale motor learning experiment (10,000+ trials) using high-resolution motion-tracking data

Engineered kinematic time-series features and applied hidden Markov models to identify latent movement regimes.
Quantified individual differences in adaptation strategies, moving beyond group-level averages

Emphasized interpretability of unsupervised results

What I’d do next

Evaluate cluster stability using bootstrap or permutation-based methods

Extend the analysis to link inferred strategies with downstream performance or transfer effects

title: Projects
text:
Python · Experimentation · Unsupervised Learning

I designed and analyzed a large-scale motor skill learning experiment (10,000+ trials), collecting high-resolution motion-tracking data

I engineered time-series features and applied a hidden Markov model to identify latent movement strategies.
I quantified individual differences in strategies.
This modelling work helps us understand transitions in strategy-use within a skill learning experiment.





GitHub Repository
Python · Classification · Regression · Tree-based models

I built an end-to-end modeling pipeline to predict the adoption of a software product adoption using data from 25,000+ clients and 1.5M+ transaction-level time-series observations.
The model includes engineered temporal behavioural features from transactional time-series data (e.g., usage consistency and variability)..
I compared different approaches like regularized logistic regression and XGBoost.
The main deliverable was a ranking table of the top 10–15% of merchants for targeted marketing. I also used model coefficients to identify drivers of subscription adoption.
